A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAT-K research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The supplementary Sections 7–10 in v1 correspond to Appendices A–D in v2, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original traffic-simulation and GMM ego-planning experiments, including comparative results, ablations, and qualitative simulations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised leaderboard results for the authors' traffic model and reproduced baseline.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces SMART's supplied agent-action vocabulary with a vocabulary rebuilt using K-disk clustering on more trajectories for the leaderboard model. This changes a model component, while the CAT-K selection procedure, recovery targets, losses, and policy architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multi-agent traffic simulation and GMM ego-motion planning using WOMD and the WOSAC setup. More trajectories for vocabulary construction do not establish new dataset, population, or task coverage; the additional applications mentioned in v2 are future work.

E2.justification: The comparison methods in the leaderboard, fine-tuning, and ego-policy experiments remain the same. Appendix D.1 explicitly identifies UniMM as the previously named MM-GPT; Table 4 updates and consolidates its historical submission entries rather than introducing a distinct comparison method.

E3.justification: Traffic-model BC pre-training changes from a reported 64 epochs to 32 epochs in Sections 5.1 and 5.3.2 and the implementation appendix. Vocabulary construction also uses more trajectories. These are reported setting changes; the unchanged ablation values do not establish whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The K-sensitivity studies, rollout and augmentation comparisons, hard-assignment experiment, and parking-lot case study are retained. Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 and Figures 3–6 provide the same analyses; v2 does not add a separate controlled vocabulary ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting without training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The 32 simulated rollouts used for evaluation are already specified in v1.

E6.justification: Leaderboard results are revised: Table 1 reports CAT-K RMM changing from 0.7635 to 0.7702 and kinematic score from 0.4621 to 0.4931. Table 4 changes the reproduced baseline's RMM from 0.7607 to 0.7671 and updates MM-GPT/UniMM results. Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 retain identical entries and values. The leaderboard updates involve revised configurations, so they are not unchanged-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The deterministic-dynamics assumption, policy factorization, and Equations 1–5 remain unchanged. The added explanation of CAT-K as a greedy approximation over possible rollouts is conceptual; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding contribution statement retain the same claims: supervised closed-loop CAT-K fine-tuning, a 7M model outperforming the 102M model, leaderboard leadership, and applicability to GMM ego planning. Revised leaderboard margins strengthen the reported evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now explicitly conditions CAT-K's effectiveness on the top-K policy rollouts covering the ground-truth mode, replacing an efficiency-only explanation for pre-training. Section 4.3 explains the greedy approximation, and Section 5.1 reports a vocabulary-based remedy for the kinematic weakness left unresolved in v1.

D1.justification: v2 specifies vocabulary sizes and token geometry, the bounding-box-corner distance metric, and the ego policy's 3.2M parameters and separate training. The appendix revises reported BC training time from 64 to 32 hours and adds a project-page link for videos. Vocabulary provenance remains imperfectly documented: Section 5.1 restricts the rebuilt vocabulary to Table 1, although Table 4 repeats the updated leaderboard scores.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Data As Demonstrator, winner-takes-all training, Motion Transformer, and UniMM. Sections 2.2–2.3 and 4.2–4.3 explicitly connect CAT-K to winner-takes-all training and attribute its recovery-target construction to DAD. These refine the positioning while retaining the broader related-work framework.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and prose, expands selected explanations, and changes supplementary section numbering from 7–10 to A–D. The main section sequence and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same six figures and six tables are retained. Table 1 moves from page 5 to page 6, Figures 4–5 move to page 7, and Figure 6 and Table 3 exchange order on page 8. Table 4 consolidates two dated MM-GPT rows into one UniMM row; the overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution to DAD and winner-takes-all training, explains an important applicability condition, and supplies useful implementation details. Its revised vocabulary also addresses the earlier kinematic weakness. These benefits outweigh the localized ambiguity about which tables use that vocabulary, but the unchanged core algorithm and most experimental evidence make the overall improvement limited.
